extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 school districts, colleges and universities), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, disability services officers, and campus legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX compliance for students with disabilities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements describing how recipients must respond to Title IX sexual harassment incidents in ways that also satisfy obligations under disability laws (IDEA, Section 504, ADA), including supportive measures, grievance procedures, accessibility, training, and confidentiality. Focuses on K-12 and postsecondary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual compliance with Title IX and disability laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must meet obligations under these final regulations while also meeting all obligations under applicable disability laws including the IDEA, Section 504, and the ADA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department repeatedly emphasizes that nothing in the Title IX final regulations relieves a recipient of obligations under disability law; recipients must ensure accessibility of websites, services, communications, and grievance procedures in compliance with applicable disability statutes. The Department will offer technical assistance on intersections between these laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance irrespective of internal organizational structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with obligations under disability laws with respect to students, employees, or participants in a Title IX reporting or grievance process situation, regardless of the recipient's internal organizational structure (e.g., separate disability services and Title IX offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when students interact with separate offices (disability office, Title IX office), the recipient as an entity must ensure disability-protected rights and accommodations are honored throughout intake, investigation, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsible for implementation of supportive measures and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If an accommodation involves a Title IX supportive measure or remedy, the final regulations specify that the Title IX Coordinator is responsible for the effective implementation of such supportive measures (§106.30) and remedies (§106.45(b)(7)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical examples include coordinating housing changes that require housing-office action or arranging re-taking an exam via the academic affairs office; the Coordinator must ensure the needed service is actually delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt offer and discussion of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures as part of a prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response to sexual harassment; the Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact the complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes, inform of availability with or without a formal complaint, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint (§106.44(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory procedural step in the recipient's response. Supportive measures are to be offered even if the complainant does not file a formal complaint; the Coordinator must document outreach and consideration of the complainant's stated preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded 'actual knowledge' in elementary/secondary context
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'actual knowledge' is expanded to include notice to any employee of an elementary or secondary school (§106.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In K-12 settings, a report to a school employee (including disability office staff or a teaching aide) triggers the recipient's Title IX response obligations; this broadens the pool of employees whose notice creates actual knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of communications, evidence, and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure accessibility of websites, services, written communications, evidence review, and hearing processes in compliance with disability laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples requested by commenters (and encompassed by disability-law compliance) include accessible formatting of written/recorded documentation, plain-language materials for intellectual disabilities, provision of materials in alternate formats, and ensuring electronic evidence review is accessible. Recipients must provide evidence in electronic or hard copy formats and in formats that comply with disability laws (§106.45(b)(5)(vi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence in accessible formats (electronic or hard copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must send to each party and the party's advisor, if any, the evidence subject to inspection and review in an electronic format or a hard copy, and should provide such evidence in a format that complies with any applicable disability laws (§106.45(b)(5)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations removed a requirement to use a file-sharing platform and explicitly permit either electronic or hard copy distribution; recipients are responsible for ensuring the provided format is accessible to the party's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow temporary delays or limited extensions for accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Good cause for temporary delays or limited extensions of time frames in the grievance process may include 'the need for language assistance or accommodation of disabilities' (§106.45(b)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must be prepared to grant reasonable time adjustments when a disability or language need makes standard timeframes infeasible (e.g., need for additional time to review evidence in an accessible format).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on impartiality and avoidance of bias, including disability bias
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requires Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and persons who facilitate informal resolutions to be trained on how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must address avoiding bias against complainants or respondents generally and against individuals (including bias based on disability status). The Department views impartiality training as protecting parties with disabilities as well as other historically marginalized groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation including misuse of non-sex conduct charges
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71(a) prohibits retaliation and states that charging an individual with a code of conduct violation that does not involve sexual harassment but arises out of the same facts or circumstances as a report or formal complaint of sexual harassment for the purpose of interfering with rights under Title IX constitutes retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include charging a complainant with underage drinking or consensual sexual activity to deter Title IX complaints. This protection applies to both complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process requirements apply equally to parties with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not permit disciplinary sanctions against any respondent for Title IX sexual harassment without the recipient first following the §106.45 grievance process, which incorporates fundamental principles of due process, and §106.45 applies equally to individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure that individuals with disabilities receive the same procedural protections and that any modification for disabilities still preserves the integrity of due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of disabilities in assessing harassment and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether conduct rises to actionable harassment depends on a 'constellation of surrounding circumstances' which include any disability of the person accused or the reporting student; recipients may consider disabilities when evaluating whether conduct is 'severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive' and when tailoring sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disability-related circumstances are relevant both to threshold determinations and to deciding appropriate consequences; recipients may opt for counseling or behavioral interventions rather than disciplinary sanctions where a respondent unintentionally committed conduct due to disability, while still providing remedies to the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support person and advisor accommodations consistent with disability law and confidentiality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with any disability laws that require allowing a person with a disability to be accompanied throughout a grievance process by a support person, in addition to the party's advisor of choice, and must keep identities confidential under §106.71(a) except where permitted by FERPA, required by law, or necessary to conduct the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may be required under disability laws to permit a support person; confidentiality obligations and FERPA exceptions must be balanced with any accommodation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child Find and IDEA-related obligations apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with applicable legal obligations under disability laws including Child Find mandates under the IDEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The obligation to comply with IDEA (including identification and services for students needing special education) applies alongside Title IX responsibilities; recipients should coordinate obligations without assuming different standards across educational levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new regulatory requirement to train on disability-specific topics or to collect demographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to impose in these final regulations a requirement that recipients train employees specifically on meeting the needs of students with disabilities or on the intersection of Title IX, ADA, and IDEA, and declined to require recipients to collect and analyze demographic or disability data about complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not prohibited from offering such training or self-study data analysis; the Department encourages voluntary self-evaluation but does not mandate it in these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflicts of interest for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) prohibits conflicts of interest on the part of Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, or persons who facilitate informal resolution processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a particular dual role (e.g., Title IX Coordinator also serving as ADA compliance officer) constitutes a prohibited conflict is fact-specific; recipients should seek technical assistance to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and reasonable modifications for hearings and technology use
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with disability laws with respect to holding live hearings in separate rooms, virtual hearing technology, and any portion of the proceeding that requires use of technology (e.g., testimony via video, evidence review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include guaranteeing accessible technology for same-room or separate-room hearings, providing assistive devices or accessible video platforms, and ensuring that remote participation does not disadvantage parties with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and notification about disability accommodations and consent to share
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may notify students involved in a Title IX grievance process that they may have rights to disability accommodations and may consider processes (with respect to confidentiality) for students to permit consultation between discipline and disability offices (e.g., advance permission to share disability information for disciplinary proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the regulations do not require a specific waiver regime, recipients may adopt intake or enrollment forms that ask parties whether they consent to sharing disability information in the event of disciplinary proceedings; such waivers must be informed and comply with privacy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide alternative complaint and communication modalities for individuals unable to use written procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with disability laws that may require offering reasonable accommodations to complainants who are unable to submit a written complaint (for example, due to a physical disability) and may need alternative modalities such as oral, manual, augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) techniques, or assistive technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should be prepared to accept complaints and disclosures in multiple formats (oral, AAC, sign language, picture boards, speech-generating devices) and to make documents available in accessible formats so parties with communication disabilities can meaningfully participate.
